what_each_pathway_assumes.direct: Ahmad Case 2a system efficiency 49.12 % on LHV 18.8 = 9.2346 MJ electricity per kg NH3 = 49.64 % on the AmCraX LHV 18.60 MJ/kg.
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_fired / partial_fired: Cracker heat = stored Aspen reactor + pre-heater duty (3.291 MJ per kg NH3 cracked) supplied by burning extra NH3 at 100 % heat-transfer efficiency (assumption, favourable to cracking). Combined cycle on the H2/N2(/NH3) fuel gas LHV at eta_h2_fuel = 49.64 % (copy of the direct value; assumption eta_gt_gas).
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_purified / blend_purified: Stored Aspen baseline cracker + PSA (recovery 0.85); heat deficit after tail-gas firing from extra NH3; combined cycle on the H2 (or NH3 + H2 blend) LHV at eta_h2_fuel = 49.64 % (assumption).
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_exhaust / partial_exhaust: Electricity per kg NH3 from Ahmad's two system end points (49.12 % and about 54 % on LHV 18.8, i.e. 49.64 % and 54.58 % on LHV 18.60, +4.93 pp), linear in the cracked share (assumption). No extra NH3 for cracker heat (exhaust supplies it) and ETA_GT_GAS is NOT used. The implied combined-cycle efficiency on cracked-gas LHV is 47.78 % (below 49.64 %, because exhaust heat goes to the cracker instead of the steam cycle).
what_each_pathway_assumes.double_counting_check: Ahmad's efficiency gain enters only the exhaust-heated kinds through eta_exhaust_integrated(); those kinds neither add cracker-heat NH3 nor apply ETA_GT_GAS, and the fired/purified kinds never use the Ahmad 54 % value. Nothing is counted twice (validation EU-P2-no-double-count).
what_each_pathway_assumes.brief_correction: The statement that all four stored power costs assume a 49.64 % hydrogen-rich turbine is true for fired cracking (280.1) and cracking + PSA (310.2) only. The exhaust-heated value (255.6) uses Ahmad's 54 % system efficiency.

statement_of_result.text: On the unified reference scenario (grey NH3 450 USD/t, 8000 h/yr, 10 %, 25 y), direct NH3 combustion gives 258.9 USD/MWh. It is 7.6 % cheaper than a standalone fired cracker (280.1) and 16.5 % cheaper than cracking + PSA (310.2), as 1 - direct/cracking, ON THE ASSUMPTION that the turbine reaches the direct-NH3 efficiency (49.64 %) on the H2-rich fuel. Against an exhaust-heated cracker (Ahmad's +4.93 pp system gain) direct use is 1.3 % dearer (255.6).

old_pre_unification.source: Phase 1 end-use results of the 23 November 2026 release (LCOE 259 / 273 / 304 / 248 USD/MWh), quoted as about 5 to 15 %

exhaust_heated_system_delta_pp.basis: combined-cycle system efficiency on NH3 LHV supplied, exhaust-heated cracker; Ahmad 4.4-5.4 pp on LHV 18.8 rescaled by 18.8/18.6; Karpilov unit and basis not stated ('up to', a maximum over TIT 800-1200 C)

fired_H2N2_fuel_delta_pp.basis: nothing sourced for a turbine on H2/N2 from a standalone fired cracker. Bracket for orientation only: lower = Ahmad exhaust-heated implied efficiency on cracked-gas LHV (derived here, exhaust heat diverted to the cracker); upper = NETL 2023 vs 2024 pure H2 (steam-diluted) minus NH3, +7.3 pp, which the literature note says NOT to use for cracked gas.

purified_H2_fuel_delta_pp.basis: NETL 2023 (66.9 %, 100 % H2 steam-diluted, Exhibit 4-9) minus NETL 2024 (59.6 %, 100 % NH3, Exhibit 4-6), same agency method and B32A baseline, H-class-like. Steam dilution inflates the H2 figure, so it is an UPPER bound for dry H2 firing. No lower-side source.

The 'loss is larger when H2 is an intermediate fuel' half: with the NETL +7.3 pp upper bound applied absolutely, the cracked + PSA route gives slightly MORE electricity per kg NH3 than direct; applied as a ratio it gives less. The energy ranking is not established independently of the turbine assumption.
